sentences.text: Anserimimus was a lanky, fast-running animal that was possibly an omnivore.
Although it closely resembled other ornithomimids, this species possessed more powerful forelimbs.
The thighbone, or femur, of the animal measured exactly 435 millimeters in length.
Its hands ended in long, nearly straight claws with a nearly flat lower surface.
Large crests on the shoulder and upper arm bone supported massive muscles like the biceps.
The bones of the hand's metacarpus were fused together, creating a stronger limb structure.
Gregory S. Paul estimated the creature to be 3 meters long and weigh 50 kilograms in 2010.
Other studies suggested the holotype could have weighed between 143.6 and 170 kilograms.
The species name planinychus honors its distinctive flat claws.
Fossils were discovered in the Bayankhongor province of Mongolia during a Soviet-Mongolian expedition in the late 1970s.
The genus Anserimimus was named by Mongolian paleontologist Rinchen Barsbold in 1988.
The only known species of Anserimimus is Anserimimus planinychus.
There is only one known specimen of Anserimimus, the holotype IGM 100/300.
The holotype skeleton is rather complete and articulated but lacks the skull and lower jaws.
Robert Bronowicz provided a detailed description of the species in an unpublished 2005 thesis, referencing additional material including a second partial skeleton, ZPAL MGD-I / 65.
In 2010, Bronowicz concluded that the second specimen, though closely related to A. planinychus, likely represents a separate taxon.
The function of Anserimimus's powerful arm with straightened claws remains unknown.
The unique arm structure may indicate a different food-gathering strategy than other ornithomimids, but the diet is difficult to determine because the skull is unknown.
Anserimimus was assigned to the family Ornithomimidae, a group of derived Ornithomimosauria.
Modern cladistic analysis has confirmed Anserimimus as a close relative of Gallimimus.
However, other studies have been unable to specifically determine its relationships with Gallimimus or any other ornithomimid.
Anserimimus lived during the early Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70 million years ago.
Anserimimus fossils were recovered from the Nemegt Formation in Mongolia.
The Nemegt Formation environment consisted of alluvial plains with meandering rivers, mudflats, and shallow lakes.
The Nemegt terrain was a floodplain with meandering rivers dating to the Maastrichtian, approximately 74 to 65 million years ago.
Anserimimus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
Sediments indicate a rich habitat offering abundant diverse food sources that could support massive Cretaceous dinosaurs.
It is debated whether ornithomimids like Anserimimus were omnivores or herbivores despite descending from carnivorous ancestors.
Some studies have been unable to specifically determine the relationships of Anserimimus or other ornithomimids.
It is debated whether the second partial skeleton specimen represents a separate taxon distinct from A. planinychus.
